children: , the AI-memory and storage powerhouse, climbed approximately 0.6% to $933.35 Wednesday as the global memory squeeze showed little sign of easing. Reuters reported that smaller smartphone and laptop manufacturers are preparing for tight supply to persist through at least 2027, reinforcing the pricing power now flowing toward major memory producers such as Micron.

The shortage is becoming painful enough to change how device makers operate. Some manufacturers are redesigning circuit boards, locking in noncancelable orders and even extending the life of older memory components simply to secure supply. Fairphone's CEO said memory can represent nearly 60% of the component cost of a roughly $400 handset. At that point, getting the chips matters more than bargaining over a few dollars. Micron sits on the favorable side of that equation as customers compete for constrained DRAM and NAND capacity.

The economics are already showing up in Micron's numbers. Its Mobile and Client business generated $11.52 billion, roughly 27.8% of last quarter's revenue, while companywide gross margin reached 84.6%. The valuation picture, however, is much hotter: the chart shows Micron at $933.35 versus a GF Value estimate of $636.82, leaving the shares 46.56% above that benchmark. Memory scarcity is delivering extraordinary economics, but the higher the stock climbs above estimated fair value, the more investors are betting those extraordinary conditions can last.

title: Micron Gains as Memory Scarcity Threatens Its Customers
